commits.message:
feat(style): suggest near-miss style and colour names (rich-diagnostics-un7.3) (#139)

* feat(style): suggest near-miss style and colour names (rich-diagnostics-un7.3)

A style token that no position accepts now names what it most plausibly
meant: `rd` suggests `red`, `bolt` suggests `bold`, `not itallic` suggests
`italic`. Because the suggestion is part of the StyleSyntaxError message,
it reaches onStyleError handlers with no further wiring.

The suggestion is built by the style parser, not the colour parser. Each
position has its own vocabulary: a bare token may be an attribute or a
colour, `on X` only a colour, `not X` only an attribute. Suggesting in
ColorParseError too would print the suggestion twice, because the style
error quotes the colour error. The two could also disagree, since `gold`
is near `bold` as well as the `goldN` colours.

A name counts as a near miss when it is within one edit per three letters,
and never less than one edit. Swapping two neighbouring letters counts as
one edit. Every name tied for nearest is listed, because picking one of a
tie would be a guess. Unrelated words (`notastyle`, `hello`) get no
suggestion.

* fix(style): bound near-miss cost and cover every word the parser names

Changes from the local review of the first commit:

- Cost. Only successful parses are cached, so a bad style runs the
  suggestion search again on every render. It measured 1.1 ms per failure,
  and 290 ms for a 2000-character token. The search now skips any name
  whose length differs from the token's by more than the budget, since two
  words are at least that many edits apart; results are unchanged. It also
  keeps three rows instead of a full grid. The measurements are now
  0.10 ms and 0.017 ms. No failure cache was added, because it would be
  more shared mutable state for a path that is already an error.
- Case. The colour parser ignores case, so `Cyna` is now as near `cyan`
  as `cyna` is.
- Vocabulary. The comment said the name lists were built from the words
  the parser accepts, but `default` and the `not`/`on`/`link` keywords
  were missing. `COLOR_NAMES` now sits in color.ts beside the table
  `parseSingle` reads, so the claim is true.

* test(style): drop the wall-clock bound on near-miss cost

This test asserted that a 2000-character token parses in under 50 ms. The
local medium review pointed out it can fail on a slow CI worker even when
the code is correct, and a fast machine could pass it without the length
filter. It timed the clock rather than checking behaviour. The unrelated-
word tests already check what a user sees. The cost bound comes from the
length-difference argument documented on nearMiss.
